docs.title: pyogmios
docs.text:
A Python client for Ogmios v7, the lightweight JSON-RPC bridge to cardano-node. Query the ledger, follow the chain, watch the mempool and submit transactions, with every request and answer typed.

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    epoch = client.ledger_state.epoch()
    tip = client.network.tip()
    parameters = client.ledger_state.protocol_parameters()
    print(f"epoch {epoch}, tip {tip}, max tx size {parameters.max_transaction_size.bytes} bytes")

docs.title: Why pyogmios
docs.text:
• All of Ogmios v7. All 24 ledger and network queries, chain sync, mempool monitoring, transaction submission and evaluation. Each query is a typed method: client.ledger_state.utxo(addresses=[...]).
  • Typed from the schema, checked against the chain. The 500 or so result and error types are generated from the Ogmios JSON schema, corrected where the schema and the server disagree, and checked against every block of the preview network and a local devnet. Results are Pydantic models.
  • Async and sync. AsyncClient for asyncio; Client for everything else, with the same methods.
  • Built for long-running programs. Many requests in flight on one WebSocket connection, keep-alive, timeouts, reconnection with backoff, and chain sync that resumes by itself after a dropped connection.
  • Errors you can catch precisely. Every Ogmios error code is its own exception, from IntersectionNotFoundError to the 74 ledger rules a transaction can break, such as ValueNotConservedError, with the server's details parsed.
  • A command line for quick checks: pyogmios tip, pyogmios query epoch, pyogmios follow.
  • Python 3.11 to 3.15, including the free-threaded builds. Apache-2.0.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
pyogmios Ogmios cardano-node (tested) Python 1.x 7.x 11.0.1 and 11.1.2 3.11 to 3.15, including 3.14t and 3.15t 0.7.x 5.x — 3.10 and up

pyogmios checks the server's version when it connects: Ogmios older than 7 is refused, newer warns (see the version check).

docs.title: Eras
docs.text: The types cover every era, Byron to Conway, as the Ogmios schema describes them. Checked against real blocks so far: every block of the preview network, 4.78 million from Alonzo to Conway, parses into the models and dumps back unchanged. Earlier eras (Byron to Mary) are only on mainnet and preprod, which have not been swept yet. The Dijkstra era and Plutus V4, which Ogmios 7.0.0 supports provisionally, are in the types but cannot be checked against a real chain yet.

docs.title: Schema corrections
docs.text:
The types are generated from the Ogmios 7.0.0 JSON schema. In these places, the schema disagrees with what the server sends, and pyogmios follows the server:

  1. Value: the schema rejects the ada key it requires, so every output and UTxO failed.
  2. RewardTransfer (treasury withdrawals): keyed by stake address, not by hex credential.
  3. ProjectedRewards: inner keys are bech32 stake pool ids, not hex.
  4. Byron delegation certificates: keys are 128-character extended keys (key and chain code).
  5. Genesis<Byron>: requires protocolParameters but means updatableParameters, which holds Byron-era parameters.
  6. queryNetwork/genesisConfiguration: its error is a response error, not part of the result.
  7. nextTransaction: the server requires params, even if empty.
  8. Pre-Conway update proposals have no guardrails.
  9. Pre-Conway votes by genesis delegates have no from.
  10. The JSON-RPC error message field is message, not string.

Two more adjustments make the models accept real data the schema allows: anchor URLs are any string (some registered metadata URLs are not valid URIs), and UTC times are parsed without the schema's regular expression. The test suite checks that each correction is still needed, so they can be removed when the schema is fixed.

docs.title: Optional dependencies
docs.text: • pyogmios[speedups] installs orjson for faster JSON. It is not available on the free-threaded builds yet. pyogmios keeps integers above 64 bits exact either way.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
pyogmios uses uv and just.

git clone https://github.com/Kingpin-Apps/pyogmios
cd pyogmios
just sync                 # install the project and every dependency group
uv run pre-commit install # lint and format on commit, check commit messages

Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, test:...): the changelog and version numbers are made from them.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
just check               # lint, type-check (ty) and the unit tests
just test-all            # unit tests on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 and 3.15
just test-free-threaded  # unit tests on 3.14t and 3.15t
just test-properties     # property-based tests over every type (about a minute)
just cov                 # coverage report (CI requires 95%)

The unit tests need no server: they run against a fake Ogmios that replays recorded responses. Every warning fails a test.

docs.title: The devnet
docs.text:
devnet/ runs a private Cardano network with Ogmios 7, in Docker:

just devnet-up      # a fresh devnet, Ogmios on ws://localhost:1338 (about 10 seconds)
just test-devnet    # the live tests, and tests that sign and submit real transactions
just devnet-down

Each start generates a new genesis, stake pool, DRep, committee member and funded keys with cardano-cli, written to devnet/.state (ignored by git), so no keys are committed and every run starts clean. The chain starts in Conway, with 0.1-second slots.

To test against another server, such as a synced preview node: OGMIOS_URL=ws://... just test-integration.

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
src/pyogmios/_generated is generated from the Ogmios schema pinned in schemas/:

just regen-models    # after changing scripts/build_schema.py or the pinned schema

Never edit it by hand; CI fails if it differs from what the schema generates. Where the schema and the server disagree, add a documented correction to CORRECTIONS in scripts/build_schema.py, with the evidence, and a fixture that proves it.

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text:
tests/fixtures holds real responses recorded from a preview node:

just record-fixtures   # OGMIOS_URL, default ws://localhost:1337

just sweep checks blocks from across a whole chain against the schema and the models (just sweep --full checks every block).

uv run mkdocs serve    # http://127.0.0.1:8000

Every Python example in the docs is compiled by the unit tests; examples marked <!-- test: run --> run against the devnet in CI.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: just bump makes the version and changelog from the commits and tags the release; pushing the v* tag publishes to PyPI and the docs to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install pyogmios

Or with uv: uv add pyogmios. For faster JSON, add the speedups extra (pip install "pyogmios[speedups]", which installs orjson; not available on the free-threaded builds).

pyogmios needs Python 3.11 or newer.

docs.title: Run Ogmios
docs.text:
pyogmios talks to an Ogmios v7 server connected to a cardano-node. Any of these works:

  • Your own node. Install Ogmios (releases, or brew install cardanosolutions/formulas/ogmios on macOS) and point it at your node's socket: ogmios --node-socket /path/to/node.socket --node-config /path/to/config.json.
  • Docker. The cardanosolutions/cardano-node-ogmios image runs a node and Ogmios together, for mainnet, preprod or preview.
  • A local devnet. The pyogmios repository has one that starts in seconds: see Testing with the devnet.
  • A hosted provider. Pass its URL, and any API key header with headers=.

Ogmios listens on ws://localhost:1337 by default; curl localhost:1337/health shows its version, network and sync progress.

docs.text:

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    print("connected to", client.server_health.version, "on", client.server_health.network)
    print("epoch", client.ledger_state.epoch())
    print("tip", client.network.tip())
    for summary in client.ledger_state.era_summaries():

import asyncio

import pyogmios


async def main() -> None:
    async with pyogmios.AsyncClient("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
        epoch, tip, height = await asyncio.gather(
            client.ledger_state.epoch(),
            client.network.tip(),
            client.network.block_height(),
        )
        print(f"epoch {epoch}, block {height}, tip {tip}")


asyncio.run(main())

The client checks on connect that the server runs Ogmios 7 (see version check). Results are typed models from pyogmios.types: an editor knows that client.ledger_state.protocol_parameters() returns ProtocolParameters, with fields such as max_transaction_size and min_fee_coefficient.

docs.title: Migrating from 0.7
docs.text: pyogmios 1.0 is a new library for Ogmios 7. Version 0.7 spoke Ogmios 5, whose protocol Ogmios 6 and 7 replaced, so there is no compatibility layer: code written for 0.7 needs rewriting. It usually gets much shorter.

docs.title: What changed

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
Ogmios 6 renamed and regrouped the queries. The closest 1.0 equivalents of 0.7's:

0.7 1.0 block_height client.network.block_height() chain_tip client.network.tip() ledger_tip client.ledger_state.tip() current_epoch client.ledger_state.epoch() current_protocol_parameters client.ledger_state.protocol_parameters() proposed_protocol_parameters removed by Ogmios 6.14; see client.ledger_state.governance_proposals() delegations_and_rewards client.ledger_state.reward_account_summaries(keys=[...]) era_start, era_summaries client.ledger_state.era_start(), client.ledger_state.era_summaries() genesis_config client.network.genesis_configuration(era=...) non_myopic_member_rewards client.ledger_state.projected_rewards(stake=[...]) pool_ids, pool_parameters client.ledger_state.stake_pools(), filtered with stake_pools=[...] pools_ranking client.ledger_state.projected_rewards(...) rewards_provenance client.ledger_state.rewards_provenance() or stake_pools_performances() stake_distribution client.ledger_state.live_stake_distribution() system_start client.network.start_time() utxo client.ledger_state.utxo(addresses=[...]) or utxo(output_references=[...])

docs.title: Transactions and the mempool
docs.text:
• submit_tx is client.submit_transaction(cbor), and each ledger rejection is its own exception.
  • evaluate_tx is client.evaluate_transaction(cbor, additional_utxo=...).
  • The transaction monitor is client.mempool() (every new transaction) and client.mempool_snapshot().

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: Complete programs for common tasks. Change the URL to your Ogmios server.

docs.title: Print new blocks as they arrive
docs.text:
import asyncio

import pyogmios
from pyogmios.types import RollForward


async def main() -> None:
    async with pyogmios.AsyncClient("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
        tip = await client.network.tip()
        async with client.chain_sync([tip]) as sync:
            async for event in sync:
                if isinstance(event, RollForward):
                    block = event.block
                    count = len(getattr(block, "transactions", None) or [])
                    print(f"block {block.height} at slot {block.slot}: {count} transactions")
                else:
                    print(f"rolled back to {event.point}")


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Watch an address for payments
docs.text:
Follow the chain and report every output paid to an address. Outputs in a block that is later rolled back should be forgotten; this example only prints.

import asyncio

import pyogmios
from pyogmios.types import RollForward

ADDRESS = "addr_test1..."


async def main() -> None:
    async with pyogmios.AsyncClient("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
        async with client.chain_sync([await client.network.tip()]) as sync:
            async for event in sync:
                if not isinstance(event, RollForward):
                    continue
                for transaction in getattr(event.block, "transactions", None) or []:
                    for index, output in enumerate(transaction.outputs):
                        if output.address == ADDRESS:
                            ada = output.value.ada.lovelace / 1_000_000
                            print(f"{ada} ada in {transaction.id}#{index}")


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Wait for a transaction to be on chain
docs.text:
Submit, then follow the chain from the tip at submission until a block contains the transaction.

import asyncio

import pyogmios
from pyogmios.types import RollForward


async def submit_and_wait(client: pyogmios.AsyncClient, cbor: bytes, timeout: float = 300) -> int:
    """Submit a signed transaction and return the height of the block that includes it."""
    tip = await client.network.tip()
    transaction_id = (await client.submit_transaction(cbor)).transaction.id
    async with asyncio.timeout(timeout), client.chain_sync([tip]) as sync:
        async for event in sync:
            if isinstance(event, RollForward):
                ids = {t.id for t in getattr(event.block, "transactions", None) or []}
                if transaction_id in ids:
                    return event.block.height
    raise AssertionError("unreachable")

For more certainty, wait for a few more blocks on top of it before treating it as final.

docs.title: Carry on from where a program stopped
docs.text:
Save the points of the last blocks you processed, and start from them next time. Several points protect against the latest having been rolled back while you were away.

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pyogmios
from pyogmios.types import RollForward

CHECKPOINT = Path("checkpoint.json")

points = json.loads(CHECKPOINT.read_text()) if CHECKPOINT.exists() else ["origin"]
with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client, client.chain_sync(points) as sync:
    recent: list[dict] = []
    for event in sync:
        if isinstance(event, RollForward) and getattr(event.block, "slot", None) is not None:
            recent = [{"slot": event.block.slot, "id": event.block.id}, *recent][:10]
            CHECKPOINT.write_text(json.dumps(recent))  # most recent first

docs.title: Slots and times
docs.text:
Convert a slot to a time with the era summaries and the network's start time:

from datetime import timedelta

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    start = client.network.start_time()
    summaries = client.ledger_state.era_summaries()
    tip = client.network.tip()


def slot_time(slot: int):
    for era in summaries:
        if era.end is None or slot < era.end.slot:
            seconds = (
                era.start.time.seconds
                + (slot - era.start.slot) * era.parameters.slot_length.milliseconds / 1000
            )
            return start + timedelta(seconds=seconds)
    raise ValueError(f"slot {slot} is beyond the known eras")


print(f"the tip, slot {tip.slot}, was produced at {slot_time(tip.slot):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z}")

Era summaries only reach a little into the future (the "safe zone"), because a hard fork could change the slot length.

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    for proposal in client.ledger_state.governance_proposals():
        votes = {}
        for vote in proposal.votes:
            votes[vote.vote] = votes.get(vote.vote, 0) + 1

        print(len(committee.members), "committee members, quorum", committee.quorum)

docs.title: Using pyogmios with pycardano
docs.text: To build and sign transactions with pycardano against an Ogmios node, use the Ogmios chain context from pccontext.

docs.title: Following the chain
docs.text:
client.chain_sync(points) finds where your copy of the chain meets the node's, then yields every change from there: a RollForward for each new block and a RollBackward when the node switches to another fork.

import pyogmios
from pyogmios.types import RollForward

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client, client.chain_sync(["origin"]) as sync:
    print("intersection:", sync.intersection, "server tip:", sync.tip)
    for count, event in enumerate(sync):
        if isinstance(event, RollForward):
            block = event.block
            print(
                block.height,
                block.id,
                len(getattr(block, "transactions", None) or []),
                "transactions",
            )
        else:
            print("rolled back to", event.point)
        if count == 20:
            break

With asyncio, it is async with client.chain_sync(...) as sync: and async for event in sync:.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
points is a list of points the chain may share with you, most recent first: the most recent one the node knows is the intersection.

  • ["origin"]: from the first block.
  • [client.network.tip()]: from now on.
  • The last blocks you processed, as {"slot": ..., "id": ...} or pyogmios.types.Point: to carry on where you stopped. Give several, in case the latest was rolled back.

If none is on the chain, entering raises IntersectionNotFoundError.

The first event is always a RollBackward to the intersection: treat it like any rollback, and discard anything you stored after that point.

docs.title: Rollbacks
docs.text: A RollBackward means blocks after event.point are no longer on the chain. Undo whatever you derived from them. On mainnet, rollbacks are usually one or two blocks deep, and never deeper than 2160 blocks.

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
Up to pipeline requests (50 by default) are kept in flight, so catching up from far behind runs at thousands of blocks a second. At the tip, Ogmios answers each request when the next block arrives, so there is no timeout on these requests.

For indexers, raw=True yields plain JSON instead of models, which skips parsing.

docs.title: When the connection drops
docs.text: Chain sync uses its own connection. If it drops and resume is on (the default), it reconnects as the client's reconnect policy says, then finds an intersection again from the most recent blocks it has yielded. You then see a RollBackward to that block, as after any intersection, and carry on: nothing is skipped or yielded twice. With resume=False, the drop raises OgmiosConnectionError.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Installing pyogmios adds a pyogmios command (also python -m pyogmios), for quick checks and scripts.

pyogmios health                          # version, network, sync progress and tip
pyogmios tip                             # the tip and block height
pyogmios query epoch                     # any query, by its short or full name
pyogmios query ledger-state/tip
pyogmios query utxo '{"addresses": ["addr_test1..."]}'
pyogmios follow --from origin --headers  # chain events, one JSON document per line
pyogmios follow --from 1234.abcd... --count 100
pyogmios mempool --full                  # transactions as they enter the mempool
pyogmios submit tx.signed                # hex, CBOR bytes, or a cardano-cli text envelope
pyogmios evaluate tx.raw
  • Server: --url, else $OGMIOS_URL, else ws://localhost:1337. Options work before or after the command.
  • Output: JSON with Ogmios's own field names, indented in a terminal and compact when piped (--pretty and --compact choose). Streams print one document per line, ready for jq.
  • Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 for an error from the server (its data goes to standard error), 2 for a usage error, 3 when the server cannot be reached.
pyogmios follow --headers | jq -c 'select(.direction == "forward") | .block | {height, id}'

docs.title: Clients and connections
docs.text:
pyogmios has two clients with the same methods:

  • pyogmios.AsyncClient for asyncio code: every method is a coroutine.
  • pyogmios.Client for everything else. It runs an AsyncClient on a private event loop in a background thread, so the two behave the same. It is safe to share between threads.

Open them with with / async with, which connects and closes for you. Without it, a client connects on its first request; call close() when you are done.

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    print(client.ledger_state.epoch())

client = pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337")
print(client.ledger_state.epoch())  # connects here
client.close()

docs.title: URLs and transports
docs.text:
The URL's scheme picks the transport:

URL Transport What works ws://, wss:// WebSocket Everything. Many requests can be in flight on one connection. http://, https:// HTTP POST, one request per call Queries, submit_transaction, evaluate_transaction.

Chain sync, the mempool and acquiring a ledger state keep state on the connection, so over HTTP they raise StatefulOverHttpError. (Ogmios answers them over HTTP, but every HTTP request is a new session, so the answers would be meaningless.)

For a hosted Ogmios, include the path the provider gives you and any API key header:

client = pyogmios.Client(
    "wss://ogmios.example.com/v7/",
    headers={"api-key": "..."},
)

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
On WebSocket, requests from many tasks share one connection: each answer is matched to its request by id, so nothing waits for anything else.

import asyncio

async with pyogmios.AsyncClient() as client:
    pools, parameters, tip = await asyncio.gather(
        client.ledger_state.stake_pools(),
        client.ledger_state.protocol_parameters(),
        client.network.tip(),
    )

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
Every request waits up to timeout seconds (60 by default) and then raises OgmiosTimeoutError, which is also a builtin TimeoutError. Override it per call, or pass None to wait forever:

client = pyogmios.Client(timeout=10)
provenance = client.ledger_state.rewards_provenance(timeout=120)  # a slow query
proposals = client.call("queryLedgerState/governanceProposals", timeout=None)  # no limit

open_timeout (10 seconds) limits opening the connection. Some mainnet queries, such as delegate_representatives() and rewards_provenance(), return tens of megabytes and can take a few seconds; message size is not limited.

docs.title: Reconnecting
docs.text:
When the WebSocket connection drops, every request in flight fails at once with OgmiosConnectionError (also a builtin ConnectionError), and the next request reconnects. Connecting, the first time or again, retries as the reconnect policy says:

from pyogmios import Reconnect

client = pyogmios.Client(reconnect=Reconnect(attempts=10, initial_delay=1, max_delay=30))
client = pyogmios.Client(reconnect=None)  # never retry

The delay before retry n is initial_delay * factor ** n, capped at max_delay, with up to jitter of it added or removed at random. The defaults are 5 attempts, from 0.5 to 10 seconds.

client.generation counts the connections opened. Chain sync, an acquired ledger state and the mempool use their own connections and handle a drop themselves: see Following the chain.

docs.title: The version check
docs.text:
On connect, the client reads the server's /health to check it runs Ogmios 7:

check_version= Older than 7 Newer than 7, or unknown "warn" (default) raises ServerVersionError warns "strict" raises ServerVersionError raises ServerVersionError "off" not checked not checked

The health read on connect is kept in client.server_health.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
client.health() reads /health at any time:

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    health = client.health()
    print(health.version, health.network, health.current_era)
    print(
        f"synced: {health.network_synchronization:.2%}",
        "ready" if health.is_synced else "catching up",
    )
    print("tip:", health.last_known_tip)

docs.text: wss:// and https:// verify certificates with the system's trust store. Pass ssl_context= for a private CA or client certificates.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
pyogmios logs to the pyogmios logger, and never configures logging itself. Connection problems are warnings; every request and response is at debug level:

import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logging.getLogger("pyogmios").setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

docs.title: Calling any method by name
docs.text:
The typed methods cover every Ogmios method, but you can also call one by its Ogmios name:

  • client.call(method, params) validates params and returns the parsed result.
  • client.request(method, params) sends params as given and returns plain JSON.
epoch = client.call("queryLedgerState/epoch")
raw_tip = client.request("queryNetwork/tip")  # {"slot": ..., "id": "..."}

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every exception pyogmios raises is a pyogmios.OgmiosError.

OgmiosError
├── OgmiosConnectionError        cannot connect, or the connection dropped (also ConnectionError)
├── OgmiosTimeoutError           no answer in time (also TimeoutError)
├── ServerVersionError           the server is not Ogmios 7
├── StatefulOverHttpError        chain sync, the mempool or ledger_state_at over HTTP
└── ResponseError                the server answered with an error
    ├── JsonRpcError             the request was malformed (-32700 to -32600)
    ├── ChainSyncError           1000s
    ├── LedgerStateQueryError    2000s
    ├── TransactionError         3000s: EvaluateTransactionError and SubmitTransactionError
    └── MempoolError             4000s

A ResponseError carries what the server said:

  • code: the Ogmios error code.
  • message: its message.
  • data: its data, as JSON (or None).
  • details: the error parsed into its model from pyogmios.types, when the method declares one.
  • method: the method that failed.

Catch as broadly or narrowly as you need:

from pyogmios import errors

try:
    client.submit_transaction(cbor)
except errors.ValueNotConservedError as error:  # one ledger rule
    ...
except errors.SubmitTransactionError as error:  # any rejected submission
    ...
except errors.OgmiosConnectionError:  # the server is unreachable
    ...

Parameters that do not match a method's schema raise Pydantic's ValidationError before anything is sent.

docs.text: Code Exception Parent Meaning 1000 IntersectionNotFoundError ChainSyncError None of the given points is on the chain. data holds the server's tip. 1001 IntersectionInterleavedError ChainSyncError findIntersection was sent while nextBlock requests were still pending. 2000 AcquireLedgerStateError LedgerStateQueryError The point to acquire is too old or not on the chain. 2001 EraMismatchError LedgerStateQueryError The query was made for an era other than the ledger's current era. 2002 UnavailableInCurrentEraError LedgerStateQueryError The query is not available in the ledger's current era. 2003 AcquiredExpiredError LedgerStateQueryError The acquired ledger state is too old to query: acquire it again. 2004 InvalidGenesisError LedgerStateQueryError The node has no genesis configuration for the requested era. 3000 IncompatibleEraError EvaluateTransactionError Returned when trying to evaluate execution units of a pre-Alonzo transaction. Note that this isn't possible with Ogmios because transactions are always de-serialized as Alonzo transactions. 3001 UnsupportedEraError EvaluateTransactionError Returned when trying to evaluate execution units of an era that is now considered too old and is no longer supported. This can solved by using a more recent transaction format. 3002 OverlappingAdditionalUtxoError EvaluateTransactionError Happens when providing an additional UTXO set which overlaps with the UTXO on-chain. 3003 NodeTipTooOldError EvaluateTransactionError Happens when attempting to evaluate execution units on a node that isn't enough synchronized. 3004 CannotCreateEvaluationContextError EvaluateTransactionError The transaction is malformed or missing information; making evaluation impossible. 3005 SubmitEraMismatchError SubmitTransactionError Failed to submit the transaction in the current era. This may happen when trying to submit a transaction near an era boundary (i.e. at the moment of a hard-fork). 3010 ScriptExecutionFailureError EvaluateTransactionError One or more script execution terminated with an error. 3100 InvalidSignatoriesError SubmitTransactionError Some signatures are invalid. Only the serialised transaction body, without metadata or witnesses, must be signed. 3101 MissingSignatoriesError SubmitTransactionError Some signatures are missing. A signed transaction must carry signatures for all inputs locked by verification keys or a native script. Transaction may also need signatures for each required extra signatories often required by Plutus Scripts. 3102 MissingScriptsError SubmitTransactionError Some script witnesses are missing. Indeed, any script used in a transaction (when spending, minting, withdrawing or publishing certificates) must be provided in full with the transaction. Scripts must therefore be added either to the witness set or provided as a reference inputs should you use Plutus V2+ and a format from Babbage and beyond. 3103 FailingNativeScriptError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains failing phase-1 monetary scripts (a.k.a. native scripts). This can be due to either a missing or invalid signature, or because of a time validity issue. The field 'data.failingNativeScripts' contains a list of hash digests of all failing native scripts found in the transaction. 3104 ExtraneousScriptsError SubmitTransactionError Extraneous (i.e. non-required) scripts found in the transaction. A transaction must not contain scripts that aren't strictly needed for validation, that are present in metadata or that are published in an output. Perhaps you have used provided a wrong script for a validator? Anyway, the 'data.extraneousScripts' field lists hash digests of scripts found to be extraneous. 3105 MissingMetadataHashError SubmitTransactionError Missing required metadata hash in the transaction body. If the transaction includes metadata, then it must also include a hash digest of these serialised metadata in its body to prevent malicious actors from tempering with the data. The field 'data.metadata.hash' contains the expected missing hash digest of the metadata found in the transaction. 3106 MissingMetadataError SubmitTransactionError No metadata corresponding to a specified metadata hash. It appears that you might have forgotten to attach metadata to a transaction, yet included a hash digest of them in the transaction body? The field 'data.metadata.hash' contains the orphan hash found in the body. 3107 MetadataHashMismatchError SubmitTransactionError There's a mismatch between the provided metadata hash digest and the one computed from the actual metadata. The two must match exactly. The field 'data.provided.hash' references the provided hash as found in the transaction body, whereas 'data.computed.hash' contains the one the ledger computed from the actual metadata. 3108 InvalidMetadataError SubmitTransactionError Invalid metadatum found in transaction metadata. Metadata byte strings must be no longer than 64-bytes and text strings must be no longer than 64 bytes once UTF-8-encoded. Some metadatum in the transaction infringe this rule. 3109 MissingRedeemersError SubmitTransactionError Missing required redeemer(s) for Plutus scripts. There are validators needed for the transaction that do not have an associated redeemer. Redeemer are provided when trying to execute the validation logic of a script (e.g. when spending from an input locked by a script, or minting assets from a Plutus monetary policy. The field 'data.missingRedeemers' lists the different purposes for which a redeemer hasn't been provided. 3110 ExtraneousRedeemersError SubmitTransactionError Extraneous (non-required) redeemers found in the transaction. There are some redeemers that aren't pointing to any script. This could be because you've left some orphan redeemer behind, because they are pointing at the wrong thing or because you forgot to include their associated validator. Either way, the field 'data.extraneousRedeemers' lists the different orphan redeemer pointers. 3111 MissingDatumsError SubmitTransactionError Transaction failed because some Plutus scripts are missing their associated datums. 'data.missingDatums' contains a set of data hashes for the missing datums. Ensure all Plutus scripts have an associated datum in the transaction's witness set or, are provided through inline datums in reference inputs. 3112 ExtraneousDatumsError SubmitTransactionError The transaction failed because it contains datums not associated with any script or output. This could be because you've left some orphan datum behind, because you've listed the wrong inputs in the transaction or because you've just forgotten to include a datum associated with an input. Either way, the field 'data.extraneousDatums' contains a set of data hashes for these extraneous datums. 3113 ScriptIntegrityHashMismatchError SubmitTransactionError The transaction failed because the provided script integrity hash doesn't match the computed one. This is crucial for ensuring the integrity of cost models and Plutus version used during script execution. The field 'data.providedScriptIntegrity' correspond to what was given, if any, and 'data.computedScriptIntegrity' is what was expected. If the latter is null, this means you shouldn't have included a script integrity hash to begin with. 3114 OrphanScriptInputsError SubmitTransactionError This is bad, you're trying to spend inputs that are locked by Plutus scripts, but have no associated datums. Those inputs are so-to-speak unspendable (at least with the current ledger rules). There's nothing you can do apart from re-creating these UTxOs but with a corresponding datum this time. The field 'data.orphanScriptInputs' lists all such inputs found in the transaction. 3115 MissingCostModelsError SubmitTransactionError It seems like the transaction is using a Plutus version for which there's no available cost model yet. This could be because that language version is known of the ledger but hasn't yet been enabled through hard-fork. The field 'data.missingCostModels' lists all the languages for which a cost model is missing. 3116 MalformedScriptsError SubmitTransactionError Some Plutus scripts in the witness set or in an output are invalid. Scripts must be well-formed flat-encoded Plutus scripts, CBOR-encoded. Yes, there's a double binary encoding. The outer-most encoding is therefore just a plain CBOR bytestring. Note that some tools such as the cardano-cli triple encode scripts for some reasons, resulting in a double outer-most CBOR encoding. Make sure that your script are correctly encoded. The field 'data.malformedScripts' lists the hash digests of all the problematic scripts. 3117 UnknownOutputReferencesError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains unknown UTxO references as inputs. This can happen if the inputs you're trying to spend have already been spent, or if you've simply referred to non-existing UTxO altogether. The field 'data.unknownOutputReferences' indicates all unknown inputs. 3118 OutsideOfValidityIntervalError SubmitTransactionError The transaction is outside of its validity interval. It was either submitted too early or too late. A transaction that has a lower validity bound can only be accepted by the ledger (and make it to the mempool) if the ledger's current slot is greater than the specified bound. The upper bound works similarly, as a time to live. The field 'data.currentSlot' contains the current slot as known of the ledger (this may be different from the current network slot if the ledger is still catching up). The field 'data.validityInterval' is a reminder of the validity interval provided with the transaction. 3119 TransactionTooLargeError SubmitTransactionError The transaction exceeds the maximum size allowed by the protocol. Indeed, once serialized, transactions must be under a bytes limit specified by a protocol parameter. The field 'data.measuredTransactionSize' indicates the actual measured size of your serialized transaction, whereas 'data.maximumTransactionSize' indicates the current maximum size enforced by the ledger. 3120 ValueTooLargeError SubmitTransactionError Some output values in the transaction are too large. Once serialized, values must be below a certain threshold. That threshold sits around 4 KB during the Mary era, and was then made configurable as a protocol parameter in later era. The field 'data.excessivelyLargeOutputs' lists all transaction outputs with values that are above the limit. 3121 EmptyInputSetError SubmitTransactionError Transaction must have at least one input, but this one has an empty input set. One input is necessary to prevent replayability of transactions, as it piggybacks on the unique spendable property of UTxO. 3122 TransactionFeeTooSmallError SubmitTransactionError Insufficient fee! The transaction doesn't not contain enough fee to cover the minimum required by the protocol. Note that fee depends on (a) a flat cost fixed by the protocol, (b) the size of the serialized transaction, (c) the budget allocated for Plutus script execution. The field 'data.minimumRequiredFee' indicates the minimum required fee whereas 'data.providedFee' refers to the fee currently supplied with the transaction. 3123 ValueNotConservedError SubmitTransactionError In and out value not conserved. The transaction must exactly balance: every input must be accounted for. There are various things counting as 'in balance': (a) the total value locked by inputs (or collateral inputs in case of a failing script), (b) rewards coming from withdrawals and (c) return deposits from stake credential or pool de-registration. In a similar fashion, various things count towards the 'out balance': (a) the total value assigned to each transaction output, (b) the fee and (c) any deposit for stake credential or pool registration. The field 'data.valueConsumed' contains the total 'in balance', and 'data.valueProduced' indicates the total amount counting as 'out balance'. 3124 NetworkMismatchError SubmitTransactionError Some discriminated entities in the transaction are configured for another network. In fact, payment addresses, stake addresses and stake pool registration certificates are bound to a specific network identifier. This identifier must match the network you're trying to submit them to. Since the Alonzo era, transactions themselves may also contain a network identifier. The field 'data.expectedNetwork' indicates what is the currrently expected network. The field 'data.discriminatedType' indicates what type of entity is causing an issue here. And 'data.invalidEntities' lists all the culprits found in the transaction. The latter isn't present when the transaction's network identifier itself is wrong. 3125 InsufficientlyFundedOutputsError SubmitTransactionError Some outputs have an insufficient amount of Ada attached to them. In fact, any new output created in a system must pay for the resources it occupies. Because user-created assets are worthless (from the point of view of the protocol), those resources must be paid in the form of a Ada deposit. The exact depends on the size of the serialized output: the more assets, the higher the amount. The field 'data.insufficientlyFundedOutputs.[].output' contains a list of all transaction outputs that are insufficiently funded. Starting from the Babbage era, the field 'data.insufficientlyFundedOutputs.[].minimumRequiredValue' indicates the required amount of Lovelace (1e6 Lovelace = 1 Ada) needed for each output. 3126 BootstrapAttributesTooLargeError SubmitTransactionError Some output associated with legacy / bootstrap (a.k.a. Byron) addresses have attributes that are too large. The field 'data.bootstrapOutputs' lists all affected outputs. 3127 MintingOrBurningAdaError SubmitTransactionError The transaction is attempting to mint or burn Ada tokens. That is, fortunately, not allowed by the ledger. 3128 InsufficientCollateralError SubmitTransactionError Insufficient collateral value for Plutus scripts in the transaction. Indeed, when executing scripts, you must provide a collateral amount which minimum is a percentage of the total execution budget for the transaction. The exact percentage is given by a protocol parameter. The field 'data.providedCollateral' indicates the amount currently provided as collateral in the transaction, whereas 'data.minimumRequiredCollateral' indicates the minimum amount expected by the ledger 3129 CollateralLockedByScriptError SubmitTransactionError Invalid choice of collateral: an input provided for collateral is locked by script. Collateral inputs must be spendable, and the ledger must be able to assert their validity during the first phase of validations (a.k.a phase-1). This discards any input locked by a Plutus script to be used as collateral. Note that for some reason inputs locked by native scripts are also excluded from candidates collateral. The field 'data.unsuitableCollateralInputs' lists all the problematic output references. 3130 UnforeseeableSlotError SubmitTransactionError One of the transaction validity bound is outside any foreseeable future. The vision of the ledger in the future when evaluating Plutus scripts is limited because the ledger cannot guarantee that the chain will not hard-fork into a version of the protocol working with a different set of parameters (or even, working with the same consensus protocol). However, the protocol cannot fork in less than k blocks, where k is the security parameter of the chain. Plus, Ouroboros Praos ensures that there are at least k blocks produced in a window of 3 * k / f slots, where f is the density parameter, also known as the active slot coefficient. Short story short, you can only set validity interval in a short timespan, which is around ~36h in the future on Mainnet at the moment of writing this error message. The field 'data.unforeseeableSlot' indicates the slot which couldn't be converted to a POSIX time due to hard fork uncertainty. 3131 TooManyCollateralInputsError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains too many collateral inputs. The maximum number of collateral inputs is constrained by a protocol parameter. The field 'data.maximumCollateralInputs' contains the current value of that parameter, and 'data.countedCollateralInputs' indicates how many inputs were actually found in your transaction. 3132 MissingCollateralInputsError SubmitTransactionError The transaction doesn't provide any collateral inputs but it must. Indeed, when executing scripts, you must provide a collateral amount which is collected by the ledger in case of script execution failure. That collateral serves as a compensation for nodes that aren't thus able to collect normal fees set on the transaction. Note that ledger validations are split in two phases. The first phase regards pretty much every validation outside of script executions. Anything from the first phase doesn't require a collateral and will not consume the collateral in case of failure because they require little computing resources. Besides, in principle, any client application or wallet will prevent you from submitting an invalid transaction to begin with. 3133 NonAdaCollateralError SubmitTransactionError One of the input provided as collateral carries something else than Ada tokens. Only Ada can be used as collateral. Since the Babbage era, you also have the option to set a 'collateral return' or 'collateral change' output in order to send the surplus non-Ada tokens to it. Regardless, the field 'data.unsuitableCollateralValue' indicates the actual collateral value found by the ledger 3134 ExecutionUnitsTooLargeError SubmitTransactionError The transaction execution budget for scripts execution is above the allowed limit. The protocol limits the amount of execution that a single transaction can do. This limit is set by a protocol parameter. The field 'data.maximumExecutionUnits' indicates the current limit and the field 'data.providedExecutionUnits' indicates how much the transaction requires. 3135 TotalCollateralMismatchError SubmitTransactionError There's a mismatch between the declared total collateral amount, and the value computed from the inputs and outputs. These must match exactly. The field 'data.declaredTotalCollateral' reports the amount declared in the transaction whereas 'data.computedTotalCollateral' refers to the amount actually computed. 3136 SpendsMismatchError SubmitTransactionError Invalid transaction submitted as valid, or vice-versa. Since Alonzo, the ledger may allow invalid transactions to be submitted and included on-chain, provided that they leave a collateral value as compensation. This prevent certain class of attacks. As a consequence, transactions now have a validity tag with them. Your transaction did not match what that validity tag is stating. The field 'data.declaredSpending' indicates what the transaction is supposed to consume (collaterals or inputs) and the field 'data.mismatchReason' provides more information about the mismatch. 3137 UnauthorizedVotesError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains votes from unauthorized voters. The field 'data.unauthorizedVotes' indicates the faulty voters and the action they attempted to incorrectly vote for. 3138 UnknownGovernanceProposalsError SubmitTransactionError Reference(s) to unknown governance proposals found in transaction. This may be because you've indicated a wrong identifier or because the proposal hasn't yet been submitted on-chain. Note that the order in which transactions are submitted matters. The field 'data.unknownProposals' tells you about the unknown references. 3139 InvalidProtocolParametersUpdateError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains an invalid or unauthorized protocol parameters update. This operation is reserved to genesis key holders. 3140 UnknownStakePoolError SubmitTransactionError The transaction references an unknown stake pool as a target for delegation or update. Double-check the pool id mentioned in 'data.unknownStakePool'. Note also that order in which transactions are submitted matters; if you're trying to register a pool and delegate to it in one go, make sure to submit transactions in the right order. 3141 IncompleteWithdrawalsError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains incomplete or invalid rewards withdrawals. When present, rewards withdrawals must consume rewards in full, there cannot be any leftover. You may also run into this error if the associatd stake credential is not registered. The field 'data.incompleteWithdrawals' contains a map of culprit withdrawals. 3142 RetirementTooLateError SubmitTransactionError A stake pool retirement certificate is trying to retire too late in the future. Indeed, there's a maximum delay for stake pool retirement, controlled by a protocol parameter. The field 'data.currentEpoch' indicates the current epoch known of the ledger, 'data.declaredEpoch' refers to the epoch declared in the retirement certificate and 'data.firstInvalidEpoch' is the first epoch considered invalid (too far) for retirement 3143 StakePoolCostTooLowError SubmitTransactionError Stake pool cost declared in a registration or update certificate are below the allowed minimum. The minimum cost of a stake pool is fixed by a protocol parameter. The 'data.minimumStakePoolCost' field holds the current value of that parameter whereas 'data.declaredStakePoolCost' indicates which amount was declared. 3144 MetadataHashTooLargeError SubmitTransactionError Some hash digest of (optional) stake pool metadata is too long. When registering, stake pools can supply an external metadata file and a hash digest of the content. The hashing algorithm is left open but the output digest must be smaller than 32 bytes. The field 'data.infringingStakePool' indicates which stake pool has an invalid metadata hash and 'data.computedMetadataHashSize' documents the computed hash size. 3145 CredentialAlreadyRegisteredError SubmitTransactionError Trying to re-register some already known credentials. Stake credentials can only be registered once. This is true for both keys and scripts. The field 'data.knownCredential' points to an already known credential that's being re-registered by this transaction. 3146 UnknownCredentialError SubmitTransactionError The transaction references an unknown stake credential. For example, to delegate to a stake pool, you must first register the stake key or script used for delegation. This may be done in the same transaction or in an earlier transaction but cannot happen retro-actively. The field 'data.unknownCredential' indicates what credential is used without being registered. 3147 NonEmptyRewardAccountError SubmitTransactionError Trying to unregister stake credentials associated to a non empty reward account. You must empty the reward account first (or do it as part of the same transaction) to proceed. The field 'data.nonEmptyRewardAccountBalance' indicates how much Lovelace is left in the account. 3148 InvalidGenesisDelegationError SubmitTransactionError Invalid or unauthorized genesis delegation. The genesis delegate is unknown, invalid or already in use. 3149 InvalidMIRTransferError SubmitTransactionError Invalid MIR transfer. The resulting delta is likely negative. 3150 ForbiddenWithdrawalError SubmitTransactionError The transaction is attempting to withdraw rewards from stake credentials that do not engage in on-chain governance. Credentials must be associated with a delegate representative (registered, abstain or noConfidence) before associated rewards can be withdrawn. The field 'data.marginalizedCredentials' lists all the affected credentials. 3151 CredentialDepositMismatchError SubmitTransactionError The deposit specified in a stake credential registration (for delegation or governance) does not match the current value set by protocol parameters. The field 'data.expectedDeposit', when present, indicates the deposit amount as currently expected by ledger. 3152 DRepAlreadyRegisteredError SubmitTransactionError Trying to re-register some already known delegate representative. Delegate representatives can only be registered once. The field 'data.knownDelegateRepresentatives' points to an already known credential that's being re-registered by this transaction. 3153 DRepNotRegisteredError SubmitTransactionError The transaction references an unknown delegate representative. To delegate to a representative, it must first register as such. This may be done in the same transaction or in an earlier transaction but cannot happen retro-actively. The field 'data.unknownDelegateRepresentative' indicates what credential is used without being registered. 3154 UnknownConstitutionalCommitteeMemberError SubmitTransactionError The transaction references an unknown constitutional committee member. This can be either because that member does not actually exist or because it was registered but has resigned. The field 'data.unknownConstitutionalCommitteeMember' indicates what credential is unknown. 3155 GovernanceProposalDepositMismatchError SubmitTransactionError There's a mismatch between the proposal deposit amount declared in the transaction and the one expected by the ledger. The deposit is actually configured by a protocol parameter. The field 'data.expectedDeposit' indicates the current configuration and amount expected by the ledger. The field 'data.providedDeposit' is a reminder of the what was set in the submitted transaction. 3156 ConflictingCommitteeUpdateError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains an invalid governance action: it tries to both add members to the committee and remove some of those same members. The field 'data.conflictingMembers' indicates which members are found on both sides. 3157 InvalidCommitteeUpdateError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains an invalid governance action: it tries to add new members to the constitutional committee with a retirement epoch in the past. The field 'data.alreadyRetiredMembers' indicates the faulty members that would otherwise be already retired. 3158 TreasuryWithdrawalMismatchError SubmitTransactionError The transaction is trying to withdraw more funds than specified in a governance action! The field 'data.providedWithdrawal' indicates the amount specified in the transaction, whereas 'data.computedWithdrawal' is the actual amount as computed by the ledger. 3159 InvalidOrMissingPreviousProposalsError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains invalid or missing reference to previous (ratified) governance proposals. Indeed, some governance proposals such as protocol parameters update or consitutional committee change must point to last action of the same purpose that was ratified. The field 'data.invalidOrMissingPreviousProposals' contains a list of submitted actions that are missing details. For each item, we provide the anchor of the corresponding proposal, the type of previous proposal that is expected and the invalid proposal reference if relevant. 3160 VotingOnExpiredActionsError SubmitTransactionError The transaction contains votes for an expired proposal. The field 'data.invalidVotes' indicates the faulty voters and the proposal they attempted to vote for. 3161 ExecutionBudgetOutOfBoundsError SubmitTransactionError The transaction ran out of execution budget! This means that the budget granted for the execution of a particular script was too small or exceeding the maximum value allowed by the protocol. The field 'data.budgetUsed' indicates the actual execution units used by the validator before it was interrupted. 3162 InvalidHardForkVersionBumpError SubmitTransactionError The new proposed version for a hard-fork isn't a valid version bump. The version (major, minor, patch) follows strict rules which can be summarized as follow: (1) the new triplet must be greater than the current one in the usual order of priorities (i.e. 'major' -> 'minor' -> 'patch'), (2) 'minor' must be 0 if 'major' is bumped, (3) 'minor' can only be bumped in increments of 1 and only if 'major' isn't bumped and (4) 'major' can only be bumped in increments of 1. The field 'data.proposedVersion' indicates the (invalid) version in the submitted proposal whereas 'data.currentVersion' indicates the current protocol version. 3163 ConstitutionGuardrailsHashMismatchError SubmitTransactionError The provided constitution guardrails hash doesn't match the expected on defined in the constitution. Some governance actions such as treasury withdrawals or protocol parameters updates must correctly refer to the constitution guardrails hash digest. The latter can be 'null'. The field 'data.providedHash' indicates the hash provided in the proposal, and the field 'data.expectedHash' the one specified in the constitution 3164 ConflictingInputsAndReferencesError SubmitTransactionError Identical UTxO references were found in both the transaction inputs and references. This is redundant and no longer allowed by the ledger. Indeed, if the a UTxO is present in the inputs set, it is already in the transaction context. The field 'data.conflictingReferences' contains the culprit references present in both sets. 3165 UnauthorizedGovernanceActionError SubmitTransactionError The ledger is still in a bootstrapping phase. During that phase, only protocol parameters changes, hard fork initiations and info actions are authorized. The transaction contains other types of governance action and was therefore rejected 3166 ReferenceScriptsTooLargeError SubmitTransactionError (code 3166) 3167 UnknownVotersError SubmitTransactionError Some voters in the transaction are unknown. Voters must correspond to registered credentials present in the ledger. They can possibly be registered in the same block, but it must imperatively happens before they are used for voting. The field 'data.unknownVoters' indicates the credentials that couldn't be mapped to any known voter. 3168 EmptyTreasuryWithdrawalError SubmitTransactionError Some proposals contain empty treasury withdrawals, which is pointless and a waste of resources. 3169 PointerAddressInCollateralReturnError SubmitTransactionError The collateral return output contains a pointer address, which is not permitted in the Dijkstra era. 3170 StakePoolVRFKeyAlreadyRegisteredError SubmitTransactionError Stake pool can (no longer) re-use an already used VRF key. Yet this transaction contains a pool which declares a VRF key that is already in use. 3997 UnexpectedMempoolError SubmitTransactionError A transaction was rejected due to custom rules that prevented it from entering the mempool. A justification is given as 'data.error'. 3998 UnrecognizedCertificateTypeError SubmitTransactionError Unrecognized certificate type. This error is a placeholder due to how internal data-types are modeled. If you ever run into this, please report the issue as you've likely discoverd a critical bug... 4000 MustAcquireMempoolFirstError MempoolError The mempool must be acquired (acquireMempool) before this request. -32600 InvalidRequestError JsonRpcError Ogmios uses this code for unknown methods and invalid params as well. -32601 MethodNotFoundError JsonRpcError The method does not exist. (Ogmios usually answers -32600 for this.) -32602 InvalidParamsError JsonRpcError The params are invalid for the method. -32602 TransactionDeserialisationError InvalidParamsError The transaction could not be decoded in any era. data lists the decoder errors. -32603 InternalError JsonRpcError The server failed while handling the request. -32700 ParseError JsonRpcError The server could not parse the request as JSON.

docs.title: The ledger at a point
docs.text:
client.ledger_state_at(point) acquires the ledger as it was at point. Every ledger query on it then answers for that point, however far the chain has moved on:

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    tip = client.network.tip()
    with client.ledger_state_at(tip) as ledger:
        epoch = ledger.epoch()
        parameters = ledger.protocol_parameters()
        pools = ledger.stake_pools()
    print(f"at {tip}: epoch {epoch}, {len(pools)} pools, protocol {parameters.version.major}")

With asyncio, it is async with client.ledger_state_at(point) as ledger: and await ledger.epoch().

Use it when several answers must agree with each other: queries on client.ledger_state each answer for the tip at that moment, and the tip can move between two of them.

docs.title: How far back
docs.text: Nodes keep only the recent ledger states, roughly the last 2160 blocks (about 12 hours on mainnet). Acquiring an older point, or one not on the chain, raises AcquireLedgerStateError. An acquired state can also become too old while you hold it; queries then raise AcquiredExpiredError: acquire it again.

docs.title: Its own connection
docs.text: In Ogmios, an acquired ledger state applies to every query on the connection. So ledger_state_at opens a connection of its own, and the client's other queries keep answering for the tip. When the block ends, the state is released and the connection closed.

docs.title: The mempool
docs.text: The mempool holds transactions the node has accepted but not yet put in a block. pyogmios reads it two ways, each on its own connection.

docs.title: Every new transaction
docs.text:
client.mempool() yields each transaction as it enters the mempool, once, then waits for more:

with client.mempool() as transactions:
    for transaction_id in transactions:
        print("new:", transaction_id)

With full=True it yields whole transactions (pyogmios.types.Transaction) instead of ids.

docs.title: A snapshot
docs.text:
client.mempool_snapshot() takes a snapshot of the mempool, to look at as it was then:

import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client, client.mempool_snapshot() as snapshot:
    size = snapshot.size()
    print(
        f"slot {snapshot.slot}: {size.transactions.count} transactions,"
        f" {size.current_size.bytes} of {size.max_capacity.bytes} bytes"
    )
    for transaction_id in snapshot:
        print(transaction_id)
  • size(): the number of transactions, their total size and the mempool's capacity.
  • has(transaction_id): whether the snapshot contains a transaction.
  • next(), or iterating: its transactions, one at a time (None at the end).
  • acquire(): take a new snapshot. After the first, this waits until the mempool has changed.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
Ogmios has two families of queries, and pyogmios groups them the same way:

  • client.ledger_state: the ledger as the node sees it (queryLedgerState/*): UTxOs, protocol parameters, stake pools, governance, rewards.
  • client.network: the chain and its configuration (queryNetwork/*): tip, block height, start time, genesis configuration.
import pyogmios

with pyogmios.Client("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    parameters = client.ledger_state.protocol_parameters()
    print(
        "min fee:",
        parameters.min_fee_coefficient,
        "per byte +",
        parameters.min_fee_constant.ada.lovelace,
    )
    pools = client.ledger_state.stake_pools()
    print(len(pools), "stake pools")
    print("treasury:", client.ledger_state.treasury_and_reserves().treasury.ada.lovelace)
    print("start time:", client.network.start_time())

Every query returns a typed result (see Types) and takes an optional timeout= in seconds.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Queries that take parameters have keyword arguments. Where a parameter holds objects, you can pass the model from pyogmios.types or a plain dict, with Python (output_references) or Ogmios (outputReferences) field names. Parameters are checked before anything is sent: a typo raises a Pydantic ValidationError.

utxos = client.ledger_state.utxo(addresses=["addr_test1..."])
utxos = client.ledger_state.utxo(
    output_references=[{"transaction": {"id": "a1b2..."}, "index": 0}],
)
pool = client.ledger_state.stake_pools(stake_pools=[{"id": "pool1..."}], include_stake=True)
conway = client.network.genesis_configuration(era="conway")

Leaving optional parameters out queries everything: client.ledger_state.utxo() returns the whole UTxO set, which is very large on mainnet. Prefer a filter.

docs.title: Every query
docs.text: Ogmios method Python Result Description queryLedgerState/constitution client.ledger_state.constitution(timeout=…) Constitution Query the current constitution definition (only available from Conway onwards). queryLedgerState/constitutionalCommittee client.ledger_state.constitutional_committee(timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateConstitutionalCommitteeResult Get the state of the constitutional committee (only available from Conway onwards). queryLedgerState/delegateRepresentatives client.ledger_state.delegate_representatives(scripts=…, keys=…, timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateDelegateRepresentativesResult Query currently registered delegate representatives, their stake (i.e. voting powers) and metadata about them. Note that 'params' is optional and can be used to filter out delegates. When omitted, ALL delegates are returned. Pre-defined options (always abstain and always no confidence) are ALWAYS returned. queryLedgerState/dump client.ledger_state.dump(to=…, timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateDumpResult Get a dump of the entire Cardano ledger state (CBOR) corresponding to the 'NewEpochState'. Take some time. queryLedgerState/epoch client.ledger_state.epoch(timeout=…) Epoch Query the current epoch number the ledger is at. queryLedgerState/eraStart client.ledger_state.era_start(timeout=…) Bound Query the start of the current ledger era. queryLedgerState/eraSummaries client.ledger_state.era_summaries(timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateEraSummariesResult Query a summary of the slotting parameters and boundaries for each known era. Useful for doing slot-arithmetic and time conversions. queryLedgerState/governanceProposals client.ledger_state.governance_proposals(proposals=…, timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateGovernanceProposalsResult Query currently active governance proposals, optionally restricted to specific governance proposal references. queryLedgerState/liveStakeDistribution client.ledger_state.live_stake_distribution(timeout=…) LiveStakeDistribution Query the current distribution of the stake across all known stake pools, relative to the TOTAL stake in the network. queryLedgerState/nonces client.ledger_state.nonces(timeout=…) Nonces Query consensus nonces information used to power randomness for leader election in every epoch. queryLedgerState/operationalCertificates client.ledger_state.operational_certificates(timeout=…) OperationalCertificates Query operational certificate counters of all stake pools. queryLedgerState/projectedRewards client.ledger_state.projected_rewards(stake=…, scripts=…, keys=…, timeout=…) ProjectedRewards Query the projected rewards of an account in a context where the top stake pools are fully saturated. This projection gives, in principle, a ranking of stake pools that maximizes delegator rewards. queryLedgerState/protocolParameters client.ledger_state.protocol_parameters(timeout=…) ProtocolParameters Query the current protocol parameters. queryLedgerState/rewardAccountSummaries client.ledger_state.reward_account_summaries(scripts=…, keys=…, timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateRewardAccountSummariesResult Query current delegation settings and rewards of some given reward accounts. queryLedgerState/rewardsProvenance client.ledger_state.rewards_provenance(timeout=…) RewardsProvenance Query details about rewards calculation for the ongoing epoch. queryLedgerState/stakePools client.ledger_state.stake_pools(include_stake=…, stake_pools=…, timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateStakePoolsResult Query the list of all stake pools currently registered and active, optionally filtered by ids. queryLedgerState/stakePoolsPerformances client.ledger_state.stake_pools_performances(timeout=…) StakePoolsPerformances Query details about pools performances indicators for the ongoing epoch. queryLedgerState/tip client.ledger_state.tip(timeout=…) PointOrOrigin Query the current tip the ledger is at. Said differently, the slot number and header hash of the last block that has been processed by the ledger. queryLedgerState/treasuryAndReserves client.ledger_state.treasury_and_reserves(timeout=…) QueryLedgerStateTreasuryAndReservesResult Query the Ada value of the treasury and reserves accounts. queryLedgerState/utxo client.ledger_state.utxo(output_references=…, addresses=…, timeout=…) Utxo Query the current Utxo set, restricted to some output references or addresses. queryNetwork/blockHeight client.network.block_height(timeout=…) QueryNetworkBlockHeightResult Query the network's highest block number. queryNetwork/genesisConfiguration client.network.genesis_configuration(era=…, timeout=…) QueryNetworkGenesisConfigurationResult Query the genesis configuration of a given era. queryNetwork/startTime client.network.start_time(timeout=…) UtcTime Query the network start time. queryNetwork/tip client.network.tip(timeout=…) PointOrOrigin Get the current network tip. Said differently, this is the most recent slot and block header hash that the node it aware of.

docs.text: A query the ledger cannot answer raises a LedgerStateQueryError: for example UnavailableInCurrentEraError for a Conway-only query on an older era.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: pyogmios submits and evaluates transactions; it does not build or sign them. Build them with a library such as pycardano, cardano-cli or a wallet, and pass the signed transaction's CBOR, as bytes or hex.

docs.title: Submitting
docs.text:
from pyogmios.errors import SubmitTransactionError

try:
    submitted = client.submit_transaction(signed_cbor)
    print("submitted", submitted.transaction.id)
except SubmitTransactionError as error:
    print(type(error).__name__, error.code, error.message)
    print(error.details)  # the ledger's reasons, parsed

The node checks the transaction against the ledger before accepting it. If a ledger rule fails, the exception is the subclass for that rule, with the ledger's data in error.data (JSON) and error.details (a model):

A few of the 74 rules Code error.data holds MissingSignatoriesError 3101 the key hashes whose signatures are missing UnknownOutputReferencesError 3117 the inputs that are spent or never existed TransactionFeeTooSmallError 3122 the minimum fee and the fee given ValueNotConservedError 3123 what the inputs and outputs add up to UnexpectedMempoolError 3997 the mempool's reason, such as "All inputs are spent"

A transaction that cannot be decoded raises TransactionDeserialisationError, whose data holds the decoder's error for each era it tried. Errors lists every code.

Being accepted is not being on the chain: the transaction goes to the mempool, then into a block. To wait for it, follow the chain (see Recipes).

docs.title: Evaluating scripts
docs.text:
client.evaluate_transaction(cbor) runs a transaction's Plutus scripts and returns the execution units each redeemer needs, to set them before signing:

for result in client.evaluate_transaction(unsigned_cbor):
    print(result.validator.purpose, result.validator.index, result.budget.memory, result.budget.cpu)

A transaction without scripts evaluates to an empty list. To evaluate against outputs the node does not know yet, for example those of another transaction you are still building, pass them with additional_utxo=; they take precedence over the node's own.

Evaluation failures raise an EvaluateTransactionError subclass, for example ScriptExecutionFailureError with each failing validator in details.

docs.title: Over HTTP
docs.text: Submitting and evaluating work over http:// and https:// as well as WebSocket.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Every Ogmios and Cardano type is in pyogmios.types: about 500 Pydantic models and type aliases, generated from the Ogmios v7 JSON schema.

from pyogmios.types import Block, Point, ProtocolParameters, RollBackward, RollForward, Utxo, Value

docs.title: Field names
docs.text:
Fields have Python (snake_case) names and read and write Ogmios's (camelCase) names:

parameters = client.ledger_state.protocol_parameters()
parameters.max_transaction_size  # maxTransactionSize on the wire
parameters.min_utxo_deposit_coefficient

Field names that are Python keywords get a trailing underscore: from_, json_, list_.

docs.title: Simple types are plain values
docs.text:
Types that are a number, a string or a list are aliases, not wrappers: an Epoch is an int, a TransactionId is a str, a Utxo is a list of outputs. Use them as annotations:

from pyogmios.types import Epoch, TransactionId


def describe(epoch: Epoch, transaction: TransactionId) -> str:
    return f"{transaction} in epoch {epoch}"

docs.title: Unions
docs.text:
Where Ogmios answers with one of several shapes, the type is a union; check which one you have:

from pyogmios.types import Point

tip = client.network.tip()  # Point, or "origin" before the first block
if isinstance(tip, Point):
    print(tip.slot, tip.id)

docs.title: Values and assets
docs.text:
A Value holds ada and native assets. Ada is value.ada.lovelace; each asset policy is an extra field, keyed by its policy id, mapping asset names (hex) to quantities:

utxo = client.ledger_state.utxo(addresses=["addr_test1..."])[0]
print(utxo.value.ada.lovelace)
for policy_id, assets in (utxo.value.model_extra or {}).items():
    for name, quantity in assets.items():
        print(policy_id, bytes.fromhex(name), quantity)

docs.title: Back to JSON
docs.text:
model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_unset=True) gives back exactly the JSON Ogmios sent:

block_json = event.block.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_unset=True)

docs.title: Forward compatibility
docs.text: The models ignore fields they do not know, so a newer Ogmios that adds fields does not break parsing. Parameters you send are strict: an unknown field is an error, so a typo cannot silently widen a query.

docs.title: Where the schema is wrong
docs.text: The types come from the Ogmios v7.0.0 schema, corrected in ten places where it disagrees with what the server sends (for example, the schema's Value rejects its own ada key). Each correction is documented, and tested to still be needed: see Compatibility.

AsyncClient(
    url: str = DEFAULT_URL,
    *,
    timeout: float | None = 60.0,

An asynchronous client for Ogmios v7.

::

async with AsyncClient("ws://localhost:1337") as client:
    epoch = await client.call("queryLedgerState/epoch")

The URL scheme picks the transport: ws:// and wss:// use WebSocket (every method, many requests in flight on one connection), http:// and https:// use HTTP (queries and submission only; stateful methods raise :class:~pyogmios.errors.StatefulOverHttpError).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default url str

The Ogmios server, including any path a hosted provider needs.

DEFAULT_URL timeout float | None

Seconds to wait for each response; None waits forever. Some large queries (delegateRepresentatives, rewardsProvenance) take several seconds on mainnet.

60.0 headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Extra headers for the connection, for example an API key for hosted Ogmios.

None reconnect Reconnect | None

How to retry connecting; None never retries.

DEFAULT_RECONNECT check_version VersionCheck

On connect, read /health and check the server runs Ogmios 7. "strict" raises when it cannot tell, "warn" (the default) only warns then, "off" skips the check. An older server always raises :class:~pyogmios.errors.ServerVersionError.

'warn' open_timeout float | None

Seconds to wait for a connection to open.

10.0 ssl_context SSLContext | None

TLS settings for wss:// and https://.

None transport Transport | None

A ready-made transport, mainly for tests; replaces url-based selection.

docs.title: errors
docs.text:
Exceptions raised by pyogmios.

Every exception is an :class:OgmiosError. Errors returned by the server are :class:ResponseError subclasses chosen by the JSON-RPC error code, and carry the server's code, message and data, plus details: the data parsed into the method's error model from :mod:pyogmios.types, when it matches one.

::

OgmiosError
├── OgmiosConnectionError        (also a builtin ConnectionError)
├── OgmiosTimeoutError           (also a builtin TimeoutError)
├── ServerVersionError
├── StatefulOverHttpError
└── ResponseError
    ├── JsonRpcError                         -32700 to -32600
    │   ├── ParseError                       -32700
    │   ├── InvalidRequestError              -32600
    │   ├── MethodNotFoundError              -32601
    │   ├── InvalidParamsError               -32602
    │   │   └── TransactionDeserialisationError  (submit/evaluate)
    │   └── InternalError                    -32603
    ├── ChainSyncError                       1000s
    │   ├── IntersectionNotFoundError        1000
    │   └── IntersectionInterleavedError     1001
    ├── LedgerStateQueryError                2000s
    │   ├── AcquireLedgerStateError          2000
    │   ├── EraMismatchError                 2001
    │   ├── UnavailableInCurrentEraError     2002
    │   ├── AcquiredExpiredError             2003
    │   └── InvalidGenesisError              2004
    ├── TransactionError                     3000s
    │   ├── EvaluateTransactionError         (evaluateTransaction)
    │   │   └── one class per failure: IncompatibleEraError (3000) ... ScriptExecutionFailureError (3010)
    │   └── SubmitTransactionError           (submitTransaction)
    │       └── one class per ledger rejection: SubmitEraMismatchError (3005),
    │           InvalidSignatoriesError (3100) ... StakePoolVRFKeyAlreadyRegisteredError (3170)
    └── MempoolError                         4000s
        └── MustAcquireMempoolFirstError     4000

docs.title: ChainSync
docs.text:
ChainSync(
    client: AsyncClient,
    points: Sequence[PointLike],
    *,
    pipeline: int = 50,
    resume: bool = True,
    raw: bool = False,
    remember: int = 64
)

Follow the chain from an intersection: yields a RollForward or RollBackward per step.

::

async with client.chain_sync(["origin"]) as sync:
    async for event in sync:
        if isinstance(event, RollForward):
            print(event.block.id)
        else:
            print("rolled back to", event.point)

The first event after the intersection is always a roll backward to it. Up to pipeline nextBlock requests are kept in flight, which makes catching up much faster. At the tip, Ogmios holds each request until a new block arrives, so there is no timeout.

If the connection drops and resume is on, it reconnects (retrying as the client's reconnect policy says) and finds an intersection again, starting from the most recent points it has seen, then carries on: you see a roll backward to that point, as after any intersection.

docs.title: LedgerStateAt
docs.text:
LedgerStateAt(client: AsyncClient, point: PointLike)

Query the ledger as it was at a point: async with client.ledger_state_at(point) as ledger.

ledger has every ledger state query (await ledger.epoch()...), all answered for the acquired point. Ogmios only keeps recent ledger states (about the last 2160 blocks), and the state expires once it is too old: queries then raise :class:~pyogmios.errors.AcquiredExpiredError.

docs.text:
MempoolMonitor(client: AsyncClient, *, full: bool = False)

Every transaction that enters the mempool, as it arrives: async for tx in client.mempool().

Each snapshot's new transactions are yielded (ids, or full transactions with full=True), then it waits for the mempool to change. A transaction is yielded once, even if it stays in the mempool across snapshots.
